name: Western Gulf Coastal Plain
description: Flat coastal plain along the Gulf. Inland it was prairie grassland of bluestem and switchgrass with gallery forests on the streams, now largely rice, soybean and crawfish country; seaward lie tidal marshes, bayous, lakes and oak-topped cheniers. Cajun music, Creole music and zydeco grew up on these prairies.

name: South Central Plains
description: Hilly, dissected uplands of pine and oak-hickory forest, with longleaf pine woodlands historically dominant in the south, cut by the broad Red River bottomlands of oxbow lakes, backswamps and cotton fields. North Louisiana country music and the Shreveport-area blues of Lead Belly belong to this region.

name: Southeastern Plains
description: Coastal plain dissected by streams into low rolling hills and broad, gently sloping ridges. The natural cover was longleaf pine and pine-oak forest, with cypress-gum swamp on the floodplains; today it is forest, pine plantation, pasture and dairy land. Studio in the Country records in these pine woods.

name: Mississippi Alluvial Plain
description: The flat floodplain and delta of the Mississippi: meander belts with natural levees and oxbows, backswamps of bald cypress and tupelo, the Macon Ridge terrace, inland swamps and deltaic coastal marshes. Poverty Point, the blues of the northeastern Delta parishes, Easter Rock, Isleño décimas and the music of New Orleans belong to this plain.

name: Mississippi Valley Loess Plains
description: Wind-blown silt, in places more than 30 feet thick, caps these hills and plains: steep Bluff Hills with beech and magnolia ravines in the Tunica Hills, rolling pine-oak-hickory plains, and the flat Baton Rouge Terrace. Baton Rouge swamp blues drew its players from farming communities here.

name: Southern Coastal Plain
description: Flat to gently undulating coastal plain with low-gradient sandy streams. Longleaf pine flatwoods and open savannas with pitcher-plant bogs once dominated, with cypress-gum swamp on river floodplains and tidal freshwater marsh toward the coast. On this map, the Dew Drop jazz hall in Mandeville stands here, on the north shore of Lake Pontchartrain.
